title: Adjacency ↔ Existing Navigation Contract Reconciliation
findings: The application already expresses logical destinations and route transitions through HTML anchors and JavaScript navigation.
The UI-response mapping explicitly separates application authority from physical authority and names logical door contracts such as main-door, market-door, gov-door, broker-hq-door and profile-door.
No current application contract binds the census door object IDs to those logical door names. Therefore physical adjacency candidates must not yet be promoted into runtime routes.
Additional-model adjacency candidates are currently physical-only evidence. This is expected at this stage and preserves the candidate/non-canonical boundary.
The canonical public Front door is a strong exterior-boundary candidate, but its physical object ID is not yet bound to the logical main-door contract.
Existing route behavior remains application-owned: navigation can transition between HTML pages without implying that a physically validated path has already been implemented.

The current camera rig provides logical section-to-camera mappings, while the UI-response mapping provides logical surface-to-camera/door contracts. This is useful evidence for a future physical binding layer.
No runtime code, canonical SH3D, or F3 candidate was modified by this reconciliation.
negative_findings: No evidence currently proves House 1 → House 2 physical transfer.
No evidence currently proves House 2 → House 3 physical transfer.
No route is declared physically validated.
No camera is finalized from this operation.
next_gate: Physical route validation preparation: construct a candidate adjacency graph with stable physical node IDs and explicit exterior/house boundary nodes, then compare only the logically required transitions.
